kjv: a pure river of water of life
mine: the river of the water of life
note: The TR adds katharon "pure" before potamon; SBLGNT lacks it.

kjv: the Lord God of the holy prophets
mine: The Lord, the God of the spirits of the prophets
note: SBLGNT reads ho theos tōn pneumatōn tōn prophētōn "the God of the spirits of the prophets", that is, the God who inspires them (cf. 1 Cor 14:32). The TR reads tōn hagiōn prophētōn "of the holy prophets".
Tachy here means "soon", not "fast". "Quickly" could mean either in 1611, but today it suggests speed of movement rather than nearness in time. The same phrase recurs in 22:12 and 22:20.

kjv: he that is righteous, let him be righteous still
mine: the righteous still do what is right
note: SBLGNT reads dikaiosynēn poiēsatō "let him do righteousness"; the TR reads dikaiōthētō "let him be made righteous".

kjv: Blessed are they that do his commandments
mine: Blessed are those who wash their robes
note: SBLGNT reads hoi plynontes tas stolas autōn "those who wash their robes", recalling 7:14 and the Lamb's blood. The TR reads hoi poiountes tas entolas autou "those who do his commandments". The two readings look alike in uncial script, and the choice has doctrinal weight. Context: those who wash their robes (high confidence). Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and the Vulgate read 'wash their robes', echoing 7:14. The Byzantine 'do his commandments' looks similar in uncial script (PLYNONTESTASSTOLAS / POIOUNTESTASENTOLAS) and may have been drawn to 12:17 and 14:12. The earlier witnesses and the book's own imagery favour 'wash'. Other possible meanings: (1) 'those who do his commandments' — TR, most Byzantine manuscripts (046), Tertullian, Cyprian, KJV, NKJV, cf. Rev 12:17; 14:12; (2) the washing understood specifically of baptism or of martyrdom (cf. 7:14) — various commentators.

kjv: God shall take away his part out of the book of life
mine: God will take away his share in the tree of life
note: All Greek manuscripts read tou xylou tēs zōēs "the tree of life". "Book of life" entered the TR through Erasmus, who supplied the end of Revelation by translating Latin back into Greek, using a Vulgate reading (libro for ligno). Context: tree of life (high confidence). Every Greek manuscript reads xylou 'tree' of life, as does the Vulgate (ligno); 'book' (libro) is a Latin copying slip. Erasmus, whose Greek manuscript lacked the end of Revelation, back-translated from Latin and so brought 'book of life' into the TR. 22:2 and 22:14 confirm 'tree'. Other possible meanings: (1) 'God shall take away his part out of the book of life' — TR, KJV, NKJV, some Latin manuscripts and Latin writers, echoing 3:5 and 20:15 where the book of life appears; the Majority Text reads 'tree'.

kjv: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.
mine: The grace of the Lord Jesus be with all.
note: SBLGNT reads tou kyriou Iēsou meta pantōn "of the Lord Jesus with all". The TR adds hēmōn, Christou, hymōn and a final amēn.
